conviction_note: Scale 8% (options say 14.6% but the ATM spread is 27% of mid; own median 3.0%, mean 4.5%, with ITSM peer ServiceNow -26.9% on its print six days ago), p_up 46: a slight negative lean from the peer read-through and a name that has sold 6 of its last 7 prints including two clean beat-and-raises, pulled toward 50 by a -9 vol-point call skew and a 12% short interest that grew 17% into mid-October; findings sum -1.2 and the scaled number is -0.64, the same sign and similar size.
bar: Q3 revenue $245.06M and non-GAAP EPS $0.181 (The Stock Observer preview, https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8967169), which equals the company's Q3 guide of $244.5-245.5M revenue, $59-61M non-GAAP operating income and ~$0.18 EPS (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001544522/000154452226000135/q226quarterlyearningsrelea.htm). FY26 guide $963.5-966.5M revenue, $222-228M non-GAAP op income, $0.66-0.68 EPS, adj FCF ~$265M. Company guide plus one agreeing estimate source, so the bar is sourced. Q2 beat the guide midpoint by 1.7% on revenue and op income by ~33% (55.9 vs 41-43); a +1.2% revenue beat is my fundamental read.
positioning_check: Short interest 29,267,192 shares = 12.26% of float, days to cover 2.9, settlement 2026-10-15 (published 2026-10-26), up 17.1% from 24,987,927 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/FRSH/short-interest). Shorts were building into the print: moderate, not crowded on the 18-23% squeeze cases. Baseline 25d skew -9.01 vol points (calls dearer than puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.12, ATM IV 85.5%, event-implied move 14.63% but ATM spread 0.267 of mid so the straddle is noisy. Tape: spot 14.20, 5d -4.7%, 20d +3.2%, 8.3% under the 52w high, +106% off the 52w low ($6.79). Consensus rating Hold with average targets $12-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/freshworks-inc-nasdaqfrsh-receives-consensus-rating-of-hold-from-analysts-2026-07-21/), so the stock already sits at or above most targets.

findings.finding: ServiceNow, the ITSM leader Freshservice (59% of FRSH ARR) competes with, reported Q3 on 2026-10-28 with a revenue beat, raised FY subscription and FCF guides, but Q4 cRPO growth guided to 18.5% against 20.5% reported, and the stock closed -26.9% on 2026-10-29 (150.13 to 109.67) on AI-disintermediation fears; FRSH fell only from 15.38 to 14.21 (-7.6%) over the same span, roughly in line with IGV (111.91 to 103.14, -7.8%), so FRSH has not been re-rated for an ITSM-specific punishment of any growth deceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FRSH's largest reaction in the baseline (-16.38%, 2026-02-10) came on the forward guide; the line the market punishes is forward growth. Q2 2026 EX ARR growth slipped from 25% to 24% and UBS/Wolfe questioned it on the call (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/freshworks/earnings/2026-q2).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had carried the NOW reaction across to FRSH, FRSH would have de-rated beyond the software ETF on Oct 29-Nov 2. Instead it tracked IGV, and calls still cost more than puts (skew -9). The market is treating FRSH as a cheap mid-market share-taker, not as seat-based ITSM exposure. A soft Q4 EX net-new-ARR guide would then be judged on the NOW standard.
findings.independence: NOW 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001373715/000137371526000092/erq3fy26.htm, 2026-10-28) gives the cRPO decel guide; Yahoo daily bars for NOW, FRSH and IGV give the price paths. One event, one finding.

findings.finding: FRSH has fallen after 6 of its last 7 prints, including two clean beat-and-raises in 2026: Q2 (revenue $237.4M against a $232-235M guide, non-GAAP op income $55.9M against $41-43M, FY guide raised) traded -4.32%, and Q1 (beat, 11% layoffs) traded -3.26%. Holders sell routine beats, and a ~1% revenue beat is the routine case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: -4.32, -3.26, -16.38, -1.90, -2.44, +3.00, -0.34; up_count 1 of 7. The beats themselves are in the 8-Ks (Q2: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001544522/000154452226000135/q226quarterlyearningsrelea.htm; Q1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001544522/000154452226000088/q126quarterlyearningsrelea.htm).
findings.why_not_priced: The run-in has been positive: the stock is up from $6.79 to $14.20, near its 52w high, and the call skew is -9. That looks like a market leaning for an upside print, when this name has not paid for beat-and-raise in 2026. If the pattern were priced, the skew would be flat or put-side.
findings.independence: This is the baseline's own reaction history plus the company's 8-Ks; it is not independent of the other findings' reliance on the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 17.1% to 29.27M shares (12.26% of float, 2.9 days to cover) by the 2026-10-15 settlement, while calls are bid (skew -9, put/call OI 0.12). Shorts are building into the print, which is a squeeze mechanism if Q4/EX ARR clears.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved squeeze on this name in the baseline; the one up print (+3.0%, 2025-04-29) came when the stock was depressed.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag and the late-October level is unknown. 12% is moderate, and 2.9 days to cover means a squeeze needs a clear beat. Priced positioning would show up as a steeper call skew or a run-up into the print; the 5d tape is -4.7%.
findings.independence: Baseline options block (skew -9.01, P/C OI 0.12) is a different source pointing the same way (upside demand).

findings.finding: $195.5M remained under the $400M 2026 buyback at 2026-06-30 after $204.5M (24.0M shares at $8.50 average) in H1; shares were down ~7% YTD. The Q3 EPS guide assumes ~266M shares, so continued Q3 repurchases add EPS headroom, and the near-exhausted authorization makes a new one plausible at the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $400M authorization (2026-02-26) came after the Feb print; Q2's $159M buyback quarter coincided with a -4.32% reaction, so buybacks have not moved the stock on print day.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 repurchase amount is undisclosed until the release; the consensus EPS of $0.181 equals the guide, which used a fixed share count. If faster buybacks were priced, EPS estimates would sit above $0.18.
findings.independence: Authorization press release https://www.freshworks.com/pressrelease/freshworks-announces-board-authorization-of-$400-million-share-repurchase-program/ (2026-02-26). Same company documents.

findings.finding: Monetization changes landing in Q3/Q4: the free starter tier was removed from the pricing page on 2026-07-20, an MCP actions add-on ($15 per 1,000) launched across Freshdesk plans on 2026-09-14, and AI Agent Studio sessions ($0.49/session) and a $29/month Copilot add-on were due to start billing in October. That gives the Q4 guide a new AI revenue line to include, against a loss of free-tier top-of-funnel on the SMB CX side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI attach metrics (Copilot on 70%+ of new deals) were in the Q2 release and the stock fell -4.32%; AI metrics alone have not moved it.
findings.why_not_priced: Usage-based AI revenue is too new to appear in consensus, which equals the guide; management said on the Q2 call it could not time Copilot upsell into NDR. A first number on Agent Studio usage would be new.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on fall usage pricing (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/freshworks/earnings/2026-q2); a different source for the plan.

findings.finding: Freshworks signed to acquire Torii (Israeli SaaS-management vendor, $65M raised, ~95 staff in 2023, price undisclosed, 'relatively small') on 2026-10-12, closing in Q4. It may enter the Q4 guide as a small revenue add and an op-income/FCF drag, and on the call it frames the AI spend governance story against ServiceNow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Device42 ($230M, 2024) and FireHydrant (2026, $56.9M net cash) were absorbed without a separately visible print reaction; Device42 later dragged reported NDR (Q2: 106% cc ex-Device42 vs 105%).
findings.why_not_priced: No price or ARR is disclosed, so the guide impact cannot be in estimates. If the market expected dilution, the stock would not have run to its 52w high on Oct 20-23 after the announcement.

findings.finding: CX ARR ($400M, 41% of ARR) grew only 3% reported in Q2 and is guided to low-single-digit growth for FY26 after the CX team was consolidated into India on July 1; a first quarter after that consolidation risks flat or negative CX ARR. Net of EX ($567M, +23%, guided mid-20s), it would take EX deceleration as well to break the total.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CX slowdown has been disclosed for several quarters with negative reactions each time (Q1 -3.26%, Q2 -4.32%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside what the company guided, so mostly priced; the residual is execution risk from the July 1 reorganization, which no estimate captures.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K for ARR figures; same call as the NDR finding but a different line.

findings.finding: Net dollar retention fell to 104% reported (105% cc) in Q2 from 106%, and management guided Q3 cc NDR roughly flat, saying Copilot upsell into the installed base is slower than attach on new deals; NDR has not shown the AI monetization and cannot until usage pricing bills.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NDR fell 108% to 106% to 104% across Q4 25-Q2 26, and each of those prints traded down (-16.38, -3.26, -4.32).
findings.why_not_priced: Guided flat, so a flat print is priced; after the NOW reaction a further step down (103% reported) would be punished harder, but that is a tail and not the base case.
findings.independence: Same Q2 documents as the CX finding; separate metric.

findings.finding: FRSH traded 18.5M shares on 2026-10-06 and 48.6M on 2026-10-07 (about 4x and 10x the ~4-5M norm) with the price flat at 13.60-13.76, and no 8-K, 13D/13G or Form 4 in EDGAR explains it. A block distribution by a holder or a large repurchase are both possible, so the sign is unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: If it was company repurchase, the Q3 release's subsequent-events or the 10-Q would reveal a larger buyback than modelled; if it was a holder exit, supply is spent. Neither is known.
findings.independence: EDGAR full-text search 2026-10-01..11-03 shows only routine Form 4s (https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22Freshworks%22&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-10-01&enddt=2026-11-03).

findings.finding: The company's EX target of 'more than $600M ARR exiting 2026' from $567M at Q2 needs only ~$17M of EX net new ARR per quarter in H2, against ~$26M a quarter implied by the trailing +23% growth; the published EX bar is conservative, and a Q3 EX ARR near $595M would sit well ahead of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EX ARR printed +24-25% in Q1/Q2 and the stock fell both times; this line has not paid on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's guide and visible arithmetic, so mostly priced; the residual is that a sell side anchored on '>600M' may model below the run rate.
findings.independence: Refresh 2026 analyst session (https://quartr.com/events/freshworks-inc-frsh-refresh-2026-financial-analyst-session_ojMIvKgj, 2026-05-14): EX expected at ~60% of ARR exiting 2026, mid-20s growth.

outside_window.finding: Atlassian (Jira Service Management, a direct ITSM competitor) reports FQ1'27 after the close on 2026-11-05, after FRSH's exit window closes at the 2026-11-04 close.
Torii deal close (expected Q4 2026) and its first contribution, plus FY27 guide (given in February), sit after the window.

baseline_tension: My lean is mildly negative (peer ServiceNow -26.9% on a decel guide; FRSH sells beats) against a -9 call skew, a 12% building short, and a stock that doubled off its lows into the print, so the findings cut against the skew and I pulled p_up from 45 to 46 and shrank the two negatives.
